subject.title: active-memory recall sub-agent gets 0 assembled messages, always times out

question: Should this issue be considered fixed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100176's half-open circuit-breaker mitigation, or should it stay open for live proof of the zero-output Codex/lossless-claw failure after that mitigation?
rationale: Current source disproves the strongest empty-prompt inference but does not prove the payloads=0 root cause; the linked PR is a latency mitigation with closing syntax, so maintainer intent is needed before the issue can close after merge.

options.title: Keep through mitigation review
options.body: Review the linked PR as a scoped timeout-tax mitigation and keep this issue open until runtime proof or a maintainer comment narrows the remaining zero-output work.

options.title: Accept mitigation as enough
options.body: If maintainers only want to cap repeated stalls, merge the linked PR with explicit proof and let it close this issue.

options.title: Split root-cause follow-up
options.body: After the mitigation lands, open or designate a narrower issue for Codex/lossless-claw payloads=0 if live evidence still reproduces it.

recommendation.title: Keep through mitigation review
recommendation.body: Review the linked PR as a scoped timeout-tax mitigation and keep this issue open until runtime proof or a maintainer comment narrows the remaining zero-output work.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and substantially evolved Active Memory recall behavior, so they are the strongest history-based owner for deciding whether the mitigation satisfies the plugin bug.
